Anovia (formerly Innovatia Technical Services) is an industry-leading technology outsourcing support provider with expertise in the telecommunications industry. Operating for over 20 years, we specialize in workflow and knowledge processes, as well as technical support, helpdesk and multilingual support services. With over 200 professional experts across the globe, we service some of the worlds’ most successful Fortune 500 and Fortune 1000 companies.

About the Role

Anovia is looking for a Project Engineer to deliver Microsoft 365, identity, and migration projects for our clients. This is hands-on cloud engineering, not advisory work: you build and harden tenants, untangle hybrid identity, manage devices through Intune, and move mail, files, and users between platforms without losing data or a weekend.

You will work across many client tenants at once, typically with two to five projects running in parallel at different stages. Each project is yours to execute — discovery, build, pilot, cutover, handover — with a senior engineer available for architecture calls.

The experience bar

• 5-10 years in IT overall, with at least 2 years administering Microsoft 365 and Entra IDacross more than one organization or tenant.

• At least five migrations you personally executed— mailbox, tenant-to-tenant, file, or Active Directory domain — with the tooling you used named.

• You own the technical execution and escalate architecture decisions. You are not expected to design a client's identity strategy from scratch; you are expected to implement one correctly and spot when it is wrong.

What you'll do

Migrations

• Run mailbox, tenant, file, and domain migrations end to end using various migration tools — discovery, pilot group, cutover plan, cutover, post-cutover support.

• Agree rollback criteria and a downtime window with the client before the window opens, and hold to them.

• Reconcile what actually moved against what was supposed to move, and chase the difference.

Microsoft 365 and Entra ID

• Run mailbox, tenant, file, and domain migrations end to end using various migration tools — discovery, pilot group, cutover plan, cutover, post-cutover support.

• Agree rollback criteria and a downtime window with the client before the window opens and hold to them.

• Reconcile what moved against what was supposed to move and chase the difference.

Azure and endpoints

• Deploy and maintain Azure infrastructure: VMs, virtual networks, NSGs, site-to-site VPN, Azure Files, Azure Backup, and Azure Virtual Desktop where clients use it.

• Manage client devices through Intune: Autopilot enrolment, compliance and configuration profiles, app packaging and deployment, BitLocker and Defender policy, update rings.

Delivery and handover

• Write the as-built documentation into IT Glue and brief the service desk, so nothing undocumented is left behind.

• Keep project time and status current in the PSA so account managers can see where things stand.

• Join client calls to explain what is changing, what will briefly break, and when.

Required qualifications

All four of the pillars below are required. Within each, you should be able to do most of what is listed without supervision.

1. Microsoft 365 administration

• Exchange Online: mail flow, connectors, transport rules, shared and resource mailboxes, mailbox delegation, message trace, retention basics

• Mail DNS: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, Autodiscover, and what TTL does to a cutover

• SharePoint Online and OneDrive: site and library creation, permission inheritance, sharing policies, sync troubleshooting

• Microsoft Teams: provisioning, guest access, and how Teams relates to the SharePoint site behind it

• Microsoft 365 admin center, license assignment, and group-based licensing

2. Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)

• Users, groups, dynamic groups, administrative roles and units

• Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync: installation, OU and attribute filtering, and resolving sync errors

• Hybrid join versus Entra join, and when each applies

• Conditional Access policy design, MFA rollout, SSPR, and why security defaults are not enough

• Enterprise applications and SAML or OIDC single sign-on

3. Azure

• Virtual machines, virtual networks, NSGs, public IPs, site-to-site VPN

• Azure Files with AD DS or Entra authentication; Azure Virtual Desktop basics

• Azure Backup and Recovery Services vaults

• Subscriptions, resource groups, RBAC, and enough cost management to not surprise a client

4. Intune

• Enrollment: Windows Autopilot, co-management, BYOD, Apple and Android enrollment

• Compliance policies, configuration profiles, and the Settings Catalog

• App deployment: Win32 packaging (.intunewin), Store apps, and line-of-business apps

• BitLocker policy and Defender for Endpoint onboarding

• Update rings and Windows Update for Business

5. Migration delivery— demonstrable experience in at least two of:

• On-premises Exchange to Exchange Online: cutover, staged, or hybrid using the Hybrid Configuration Wizard

• Tenant-to-tenant migration following an acquisition, divestiture, or rebrand

• Google Workspace or IMAP to Microsoft 365

• File server or NAS to SharePoint Online, OneDrive, or Teams

• Active Directory domain migration or consolidation: ADMT, SID history, forest trusts, UPN suffix change, workstation re-domain

• Another MDM platform into Intune

6. Windows Server and AD DS

• Active Directory Domain Services, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, file and print services

• Hyper-V setup and configuration

7. PowerShell

• Bulk operations against Exchange Online, Microsoft Graph, and Entra

• You read and modify scripts rather than only running ones you found

8. Working style

• Experience working on a fully remote team.

• Client-facing: comfortable explaining a downtime window to a non-technical stakeholder.

• Documentation discipline — across many tenants, undocumented work is lost work.

• Available for scheduled after-hours and weekend cutover windows.

• Prior MSP or multi-client experience.

Required qualifications

• Security and compliance:Microsoft Purview (DLP, retention, sensitivity labels, eDiscovery), Defender for Office 365, Defender for Cloud Apps, Secure Score remediation, CIS benchmarks, HIPAA or CMMC-adjacent client work

• Privileged identity:Privileged Identity Management, access reviews, entitlement management

• Automation:Power Automate, Power Apps, Azure Automation, Logic Apps, Graph API scripting beyond cmdlets

Helpful Qualifications

• Microsoft 365 backup and BCDR:Veeam, Datto, Dropsuite, Afi, Acronis, Keepit

• Hypervisors:VMware ESXi, Nutanix Acropolis

• Other platforms:AWS, Google Workspace administration, Egnyte, Citrix ShareFile, Cloudflare, QuickBooks Online

• Apple ecosystem:macOS and iOS deployment, Apple Business Manager, Jamf, Mosyle, or Intune for Mac

• Network and edge:SonicWall and Fortinet firewalls, Cisco Meraki and Ubiquiti wireless, Cisco and Dell switching

• Storage:QNAP, Synology, and Dell NAS, particularly as a migration source

• MSP tooling:ConnectWise Manage and Automate, Sention, Autotask, Kaseya, NinjaOne, Datto RMM, IT Glue, Hudu; multi-tenant M365 administration tools such as Nerdio, inforcer, CIPP; password management such as Keeper; M365 migration tools such as BitTitan.

Certifications

At least one current Microsoft role-based certification, or demonstrable equivalent experience. Examples:

· MS-102- Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert

· SC-300- Identity and Access Administrator

· MD-102- Endpoint Administrator

· AZ-104- Azure Administrator Associate

· AZ-800 / AZ-801- Windows Server Hybrid Administrator

· MS-700- Teams Administrator

· SC-200- Security Operations Analyst

• Robust reward and recognition programs

• Company incentive programs offered

• Attractive leave policy: Holiday Leave, Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Birthday …

About PostHog
PostHog is your product’s context layer. It ingests and stores your analytics, errors, replays, and business data so you and your agents can query and act on it.
We launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort. We've since shipped more than a dozen products, including:
• 
A suite of analytics and observability tools, including product analytics, replay vision, AI observability, and error tracking
• 
PostHog MCP for users and their agents to query and act on their product and business data
• 
Data warehouse so users can query product and customer data together using custom SQL insights.
We are:
• 
Product-led. More than 500K organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit.
• 
Default alive. Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.
• 
Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey.
We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible. 
 
Things we care about
• 
Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook. Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.
• 
Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions. Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.
• 
Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.
• 
Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days, and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had.
• 
Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun.
Other companies would call this being a Product Marketer, but we're looking for someone with devtool experience, so: Developer Marketer.
As a Developer Marketer for Sales, your job is to distil the sometimes chaotic happenings within PostHog into sales enablement. You'll be taking positioning and messaging from across PostHog and turning it into something Sales can actually use to win deals.
You'll use a mix of strong communication and engineering skills to do it. You'll collaborate closely with our sales team, our other PMMs, engineers, and users to strengthen our position as the default all-in-one devtool.
The work spans positioning, competitive intelligence, objection handling, customer storytelling, and the operating cadence that keeps it all current. PostHog ships fast and our product surface area is broad -- staying ahead of that, and making sure Sales doesn't fall behind it, is the core of the job. You'll also create positioning and messaging for platform features and areas without a dedicated PMM.
Marketers at PostHog are hands-on, T-shaped people who take on a lot of varied responsibilities to support users and other teams. You'll be one of the key voices for our company and comfortable being visible to customers, partners, and the sales team, often translating between them.

What you will be doing
• 
Owning sales enablement end-to-end. You'll be the person Sales goes to for positioning, competitive material, objection handling, and customer stories. You'll build and maintain the playbooks in the public handbook so Sales can find what they need in the moment they need it.
• 
Translating PMM work into Sales-ready material. Our PMMs own product-level positioning and messaging for some products. You'll take that work and turn it into battlecards, talk tracks, discovery questions, and enablement sessions that Sales can actually use.
• 
Filling positioning gaps. Some platform features and product areas don't have a dedicated PMM today. You'll own positioning for those areas so Sales has a clear story everywhere.
• 
Surfacing insight from real customer conversations. Use cases, objections, and pain points are currently buried in Gong recordings and Slack threads. You'll pull signal out of those and feed it back into messaging, content, and product.
• 
Shipping. A lot. This is not a job where you write a strategy deck and wait. You'll be shipping enablement every week -- battlecards, FAQs, training sessions, launch enablement -- and iterating fast based on what Sales actually finds useful.
Example public issues/projects:
• 
Product Launch: Launch Plan: LLM Observability requests-for-comments-public#348
• 
Price Cut Comms: RFC: Data warehouse pricing update Q3 2025 requests-for-comments-internal#818

What you won't be doing
❌ Writing whitepapers, mission statements, or sales decks nobody reads.
❌ Running formal certification programs or quarterly readiness training.
❌ Owning the CRM, sales ops, or pipeline metrics. That's Sales' job.
❌ Spending multiple quarters planning big projects which don't have immediate impact.
❌ Running yawn-worthy webinars and bombarding users with invitations to attend.

Requirements
• 
Excellent writing, researching, and communication skills
• 
Development experience, though not necessarily in a formal role -- vibecoded side projects still count
• 
Experience targeting developers as customers or writing for technical audiences
• 
Experience building and maintaining sales enablement content that's actually used
• 
Comfort working closely with Sales as your primary internal customer

Nice to have
• 
Experience surfacing insights from call recordings (Gong, Granola, etc.)
• 
Experience working with handbook-style documentation as the source of truth
• 
Familiarity or experience working with devtool products
• 
Experience working as a product marketer, growth marketer, or content marketer
